title: Every function takes the tenant from the caller, not from PAPYRUS_TENANT_ID
description:
Outcome: Today the functions learn their tenant from a build variable: amplify/site-backend.ts (lines 471-491) copies PAPYRUS_TENANT_ID into content-actions, category-action, assignment-action, newsroom-summary and editorial-checks, and PAPYRUS_SINGLE_PUBLICATION_BACKEND into content-actions. The schema also grants every function full access to every model (functionGrants in schema.ts: allow.resource(contentActions) and eight more). So on a shared stack a function would act for whichever tenant its variable names. Change: each handler builds one TenantContext from the AppSync event's identity claims (role claim from PPY-0bb0fd); an IAM-signed call (operator or worker) must name the tenant explicitly and is allowed only for the platform operator role (PPY-203ce2); every read and write goes through the tenant-scoped client (PapyrusGraphQLAuthoringClient(tenant_id=...) in Python, lib/tenant-keys.ts in TypeScript). On a dedicated stack the context is the fixed tenant and the checks pass trivially. Reference intake's refusal of tenant backends (docs/multi-tenancy.md, "Single-publication backends") is replaced by real tenant keys on Reference and corpora (PPY-ce6207).

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/site-backend.ts (tenant env block), amplify/functions/shared/editorial-context.ts (tenant(row, tenantId) check), handlers of content-actions (handler.py), category-action, assignment-action, newsroom-summary, editorial-checks, procedure-action, image-service, manage-user-role, model-attachment-upload, public-forms, knowledge-query, monitoring-view, automation-view, proposal-actions, reader-settings, plugins/reader-steering/function, plugins/home-page/function, plugins/newsletter, plugins/signup/function, cli-login; src/papyrus_content (graphql client tenant handling, monitoring_intake.py ReferenceIntake tenant checks); lib/tenant-keys.ts.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/function-tenant-context.feature):
Scenario: A function acts only for the caller's tenant
    Given a shared stack with tenants "alpha" and "beta"
    And an "alpha" editor
    When the editor calls saveItemDraft with the id of a "beta" story
    Then the call is refused with "not found" and nothing of "beta" is read or written

Scenario: An IAM call without a tenant is refused on a shared stack
    Given the platform operator role
    When it invokes content-actions without naming a tenant
    Then the call is refused before any read

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-0bb0fd, PPY-94d609. Blocks PPY-203ce2, PPY-bdc4ee, PPY-daf673. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-5e0259, PPY-ed33f4.

Testing: Unit tests per handler for the context (procedures/newsroom/tests/test_function_tenant_context.py for the Python handlers, scripts/test-function-tenant-context.ts for the TypeScript ones: a shared stack refuses an IAM call with no tenant, a token with no tenant claim and claims that name two tenants, before any read; a dedicated stack refuses another tenant's claim). Behave with two tenants on the repo's in-memory backend (features_backend/function-tenant-context.feature; no sandbox account exists, decision D9, so nothing here calls AWS). A lint test (scripts/test-function-tenant-context.ts) fails if a moved handler reads PAPYRUS_TENANT_ID or any other environment tenant, and its handler list is the schema's function list (scripts/generate-tenant-isolation-cases.ts), so a new function without a place in features_backend/fixtures/function-tenant-context/handlers.json fails CI; the adversarial case table gets an "IAM call without a tenant is refused" case per function.
Rollout: Releasable alone: dedicated stacks keep their fixed tenant; the shared behaviour is selected by a synth-time tenancy mode (site-backend-config.ts).
Risk and mitigation: Risk: one handler is missed and acts cross-tenant with its schema-wide grant. Mitigation: the adversarial suite calls every custom mutation and query with foreign ids, and the list of handlers is generated from schema.ts, so a new function without a test fails CI.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: changes: function code enforces tenant (schema-level function grants unchanged).
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
